content_html:
Kettle scale is mineral buildup left behind as hard water is heated. It is removed more safely by dissolving it with a compatible descaler or mild acid than by scraping the heating element. Follow the manufacturer's ratio and dwell time, rinse repeatedly, and never mix vinegar, citric acid, or other descalers with bleach or unrelated cleaners.

Check which descaler the manufacturer allows

Some manuals recommend diluted vinegar, citric acid, or a commercial product, while others specify a particular formula. Do not assume stronger concentration speeds the process without consequences; it can affect seals, metals, or coatings.

Cover the scaled area without overfilling

Add enough solution to cover the scaled area while respecting the maximum fill mark. Depending on the product, heating or simply soaking may be required; follow the exact procedure to avoid foaming, splashing, or unnecessary fumes.

Empty and rinse until odor and residue are gone

Dispose of the solution as directed, rinse several times, and, if the manual recommends it, boil clean water and discard it before drinking. Do not use the first post-descaling water if it still smells of the product.

Descale more often if scale returns quickly

Very hard water deposits minerals faster. A thin film is easier to remove than heavy crust, so adjust the interval to usage. If you see metallic flakes, corrosion, or element damage, stop using the appliance and consider replacement.
